summary: Independent review of the threshold-drift control, isolated from #964 at my request. This closes the one finding I recorded when I pinned #964: the three-bar liquidity threshold was written in two places, the watch hardcoding 3 and the strategy defining _RESTING_LIQUIDITY_CANCEL_BARS = 3, with nothing asserting they were the same number. The change is a named constant LIQUIDITY_PULL_BARS = 3, the bare literal at the comparison site replaced by it, and one test asserting it equals schwab_1m_v2._RESTING_LIQUIDITY_CANCEL_BARS. Eight insertions and one deletion, and the deletion is only the literal becoming the constant, so both sides remain 3 and no behaviour changes. This is a fix to my own finding, so I treated it as a claim I co-sign and proved the control is load-bearing rather than decorative. Mutation matrix against a baseline of 74 green: moving the STRATEGY constant from 3 to 4 while leaving the watch untouched fails test_liquidity_pull_threshold_matches_the_strategy_rule, which is the exact scenario I raised, and the improvement over #964 is specific. Under #964 that same mutation failed only the strategy's own behaviour tests, which are precisely the tests whoever deliberately changes the rule would update on their way past, leaving the watch silently checking 3 and reading a genuine early pull as guard-working, a false clean. Now a dedicated agreement test fails that cannot be dismissed as expected fallout. The reverse drift, moving the WATCH constant to 4 while the strategy stays at 3, fails three tests, so both directions are covered rather than only the one I named. Most importantly, neutering the control so the assert compares the constant to itself and then moving the strategy to 4 leaves 58 tests passing and the drift sails straight through, which is the proof that the assertion is doing the work. I confirmed no other bare 3 survives in evaluate_liquidity_pull; the only remaining literal threes are prose in the catalog spec string and the doc table, which are descriptive rather than functional, so a drift there is cosmetic and cannot produce a false clean. I did not ask for a change on that, but noted that if the row is touched again those strings should be phrased off the constant. Controlled pair, full unit suite, compared as sorted failure-NAME sets rather than counts: base 928438b 46 failed / 3771 passed, head e531124 46 failed / 3772 passed, identical 46 names, zero new failures. The base matches #964's head exactly, as it should since 928438b is #964 merged, and the +1 delta is exactly the one new test, so the numbers reconcile without residue. Both worktrees were asserted to import their own project_mai_tai before any count was trusted, because the venv's editable .pth hardcodes the main checkout's src and a worktree run without PYTHONPATH silently compares main against main. Gate: base is an ancestor of head, so no rebase is needed, and the diff is confined to the watch module and its test file. CI: validate passed twice on this head before I pinned. Nothing has been installed, activated, deployed or restarted; the weekend activation checklist still requires the operator's separate GO.
